title: Complete HTML Reference and Further Learning
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of complete html reference and further learning in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Complete HTML Reference and Further Learning” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with finding elements in the html living standard, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: This topic supports code review and long-term maintenance: recognize old patterns, check current standards, and ship markup whose quality can be explained and tested.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: This topic supports code review and long-term maintenance: recognize old patterns, check current standards, and ship markup whose quality can be explained and tested.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Finding elements in the HTML Living Standard is one of the decisions covered by Complete HTML Reference and Further Learning. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Using official accessibility guidance
items.text: Use native HTML semantics first, then test keyboard interaction, visible focus, names, roles, states, headings, and error feedback. Automated checks help but cannot replace manual testing.

items.title: Checking browser compatibility
items.text: Browsers parse HTML into a document tree and recover from many authoring errors. Browser recovery is not a substitute for valid markup; inspect the DOM and validate the original source.

items.title: Staying informed about changes to standards
items.text: Form controls need meaningful labels and names, clear instructions, and constraints that match the data. Treat browser validation as feedback for users, not proof that submitted data is trustworthy.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates complete html reference and further learning. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Complete HTML Reference and Further Learning.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for complete html reference and further learning.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: The result is a main content region with a heading, paragraph, and two-item list.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Complete HTML Reference and Further Learning is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.
Form controls need meaningful labels and names, clear instructions, and constraints that match the data. Treat browser validation as feedback for users, not proof that submitted data is trustworthy.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
